features.notes:
PAIRED with the receiver's schema-001, which was DEPLOYED FIRST and is live on master at f1085a7 — verified before this feature started, so the order CLAUDE.md fixes was respected. CORRECTION TO THIS NOTE'S EARLIER RATIONALE, checked against the receiver's source rather than trusted: this pair has no 400 in it and never did. ingest.py:214 validates `v` as _num(x, 1, 10), so v=5 was already accepted before the receiver moved, and ingest.py:159 has had `enterTick` in ROOM_OPTIONAL since schema 3. No field is added, removed or retyped here — only the meaning of an existing one changes — so nothing would have rejected this build and the 'loses every run of it' claim did not apply. The receiver corrected the mirror image of the same false rationale on its own side. WHAT THE REAL RISK IS, and it is worse than a 400 because it is silent: roomstats.py routes the clear span on the report's `v` alone (STAY_ANCHOR_SCHEMA = 5), below 5 into `clear` and at-or-above into `clearStay`, never mixing them. Shipping the stay anchor with SCHEMA left at 4 would fold every stay-anchored span back into the old sighting-anchored average — no 400, no log line, and profiles/ is append-only so the mean could never be cleaned. Hence SCHEMA 4 -> 5 in RunReport.kt as part of this feature, and a test that fails if the anchor is stay-based while v < 5. WHY IT MATTERS: the receiver's roomstats.py docstring — `clear` was an upper bound, not a duration, because enterTick was stamped the first time ANY party member was seen in the room with no minimum stay, so 145 s got reported for a 1x1. HOW IT IS ANCHORED NOW: TrackedRoom tracks a current stay per member (start, ticks, lastSeen) instead of only the run-long tick total, and enteredAtTick is the start of the first stay to reach MIN_TICKS — its own start, not the tick it qualified at, since the latter would shorten every clear in the data by a flat second. Sighting gaps of up to MIN_TICKS do not split a stay, because PartyTracker.positions deliberately reports no teammate positions at all for the 10-20 ticks around a death. A room that clears before anyone qualifies falls back to the earliest stay begun within the last MIN_TICKS: without that, the empty 1x1s that clear on entry (three in one M7, per the count in ContributionTracker.award) would carry no anchor at all and the server's mean would be built from every room EXCEPT the fastest — a bias rather than sparsity. The fallback's window is what makes it safe, since every span it can produce is under a second by construction and it can never reach back to an old walk-through. Nothing anchors after the clear, so enterTick <= clearTick holds whenever both are set, and a preCleared room now reports a null anchor for its whole life (honest: there is no clear of ours to time, and roomstats.py:102 skips preCleared rooms anyway). enteredAtTick is `private set` so the invariant has exactly one home. NOT SHIPPED: no version bump and no dist/ refresh, so this reaches no install until the next release, which is the user's decision.

THREE OPEN REVIEW FINDINGS, carried here in session 006 so they stop dying in evaluator-rubric.md, which is overwritten wholesale every pass — two reviewers had already hand-copied them forward by hand, and the one finding that was fixed in one file and left live in another (init.sh vs claude-progress.md) is what that costs. All three are non-blocking, none changes this feature's status, and none is a defect in the shipped behaviour.

(1) stay.ticks COUNTS SIGHTINGS, NOT ELAPSED TICKS — MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001. The reasoning was: the gap test is per-gap rather than cumulative, so a member sighted once every 20 ticks accumulates a qualifying stay whose start is far older than MIN_TICKS — each individual gap is within tolerance, so nothing splits the stay, while the sighting count crawls to the threshold over a much longer wall-clock span. THE REAL FLOOR SHOWS BOTH HALVES OF THAT IN ONE RUN. docs/evidence/session-1786719912927/ carries ten room_anchored events; NINE of them are stamped EXACTLY 19 ticks after the stay's `at` — which is what a per-tick decoration stream and MIN_TICKS=20 predict, since the 20th sighting lands 19 ticks after the first — and the tenth, New Trap, is stamped at 24, meaning five sightings went missing inside a window the gap tolerance did not split. So sightings and elapsed ticks coincide when the stream is clean and diverge exactly as reasoned when it is not, and the reading is a measurement rather than an inference. readout.sh asserts 9 at delta 19, 1 at delta 24, and 0 at any other delta. THE KDOC FIX THIS NOTE ASKED FOR IS NOW MADE: TrackedRoom.onPresence carries a paragraph saying ticks are sightings, with the measurement and the artifact path.

(2) THE GAP TOLERANCE IS CALIBRATED, NOT MEASURED — STILL OPEN, AND THE REAL RUN DID NOT CLOSE IT. Re-checked 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001 rather than assumed closed because a session file finally arrived. MIN_TICKS as the gap that may not split a stay is reasoned from PartyTracker.positions' documented 10-20 tick roster-skew window around a death, with ZERO MARGIN — 20 against a documented worst case of 20. If the real blackout ever runs one tick longer, a stay splits and the room anchors on the return instead of the arrival. WHY docs/evidence/session-1786719912927/ CANNOT SETTLE IT: the failure mode is party-and-death-specific, and that run was SOLO and DEATHLESS — one player in tab, roster_skew fired ZERO times, so PartyTracker's blackout path was never entered. The largest divergence observed anywhere in the run was New Trap's five missed sightings against a tolerance of twenty, which is a four-fold margin on the ordinary case and says nothing about the worst one. A real run reports what happened, not what the worst case is. Needs a party floor with at least one death.

(3) anchorOnClear's REAL-FLOOR FREQUENCY — MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001: ONE IN TEN. The fallback is bounded by construction (it can never invent a span longer than one second), so how often it fires was a question about data quality rather than correctness — but if it fired on most rooms, the anchor would be mostly a fallback and the feature would have bought less than it looks like. It does not. On the one real M7 (docs/evidence/session-1786719912927/) ten rooms were cleared and exactly ONE carries anchoredOnClear=true: Duncan, a 1x1 entered at tick 2990 and cleared at 2996, six ticks, so no stay could reach twenty. The other nine were anchored by a genuine qualifying stay. The anchor is mostly real and the fallback is the exception it was designed to be. readout.sh asserts 10 cleared, 1 anchoredOnClear=true, 9 false, and that the one is Duncan. THE KDOC ESTIMATE IT CONTRADICTS IS ALSO FIXED: ContributionTracker.anchorOnClear said 'the empty 1x1s, three of them in one M7' and two ContributionTrackerTest KDocs repeated it; all three now carry the measured one-in-ten. Same order, benign direction. ONE THING THE MEASUREMENT TURNED UP THAT NOBODY HAD WRITTEN DOWN: Duncan is also the room missing from history.jsonl, because RoomHistory.kt:144 only records a clear when the local player's own presence reached MIN_TICKS and Duncan's was 7. So that run wrote 9 local clear lines for 10 cleared rooms. That is existing deliberate behaviour, not a defect — but the fallback-anchored room is precisely the one local history drops, and anyone comparing the two files will meet the off-by-one.

features.notes:
THE USER'S DESIGN, 2026-08-14, and it replaces clearpoints-001's formula rather than extending it: '1 Secret EGAL welcher Raum = +0.25, alle anderen Raeume haben einen Base Score von 0.75, und abhaengig davon wie schnell der durchschnittliche Spieler diesen Raum cleart (KEINE SECRETS) geht dieser Wert hoch oder auch runter.'

THE BLOCKER WAS RESOLVED BY THE USER, NOT BY THE DATA ARRIVING. The entry used to read BLOCKED ON DATA - roomstats.json has 83 rooms, 9 with any clear sample, all n=1, and `clearStay` empty for every one of them. That is still exactly true today (measured over SSH against /srv/sighte/roomstats.json this session: 83 rooms, 9 with a `clear` sample, sum of every room's clearStay n = 0). What changed is the user supplying seed values and asking for the self-correcting logic to ship anyway: 'Das sind erstmal nur geschaetzte Werte, ich moechte dass die Logic trotzdem in Kraft tritt, dass sie die Werte somit immer verbessern.' So the seeds are a PRIOR rather than a constant, and the feature is the blend that retires them.

WHAT IT DELETED: PUZZLE_BONUS, TRAP_BONUS, MINIBOSS_BONUS, BLOOD_BONUS and SEGMENT_POINTS - five hand-picked constants, gone. Size and kind are emergent now: a four-segment room scores high because crossing it measures slow, not because a number says a segment is worth 0.5. BASE_POINTS 1.0 became ORDINARY_SEED 0.75. SECRET_POINTS stays 0.25 and stays keyed on the database's count rather than secretsFound, for the reason clearpoints-001 already has a test on.

THE MODEL, and every number in it is argued in the KDoc rather than only here. base = seed + w * (measured - seed), where measured = 0.75 * (avgTicks / medianTicks) ^ 0.5 clamped to [0.25, 2.5], and w = n / (n + 10). SEEDS: Ice Fill 2.0, Water Board 1.5, Quiz 1.0, any other PUZZLE 1.0, everything else 0.75 - the user's table one for one, keyed on rooms.json's spelling (two words each; a typo silently misses). SHAPE: the exponent is 0.5, i.e. four times the median clear time is twice the ordinary base. Not linear, and the reason is measured: the real clear averages span 0.75 s to 36.5 s (49x) while the user's own estimates span 0.75 to 2.0 (2.7x), so a linear map calibrated on the median would put the slowest room at ten times the base and the CLAMP would be deciding almost every room - a constant wearing a measurement's clothes. MEASURED ON A PROXY, AND BOTH KDOCS NOW SAY SO (added 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001; the KDocs argued the calibration without naming its source, in a file that elsewhere spends a paragraph insisting the two metrics must never be confused). That 49x spread is the box's `clear` averages, NOT `clearStay`, because clearStay has n=0 for every room on the box and therefore has no spread to measure. `clear` is the walk-through-inflated upper bound clearStay exists to replace, and the inflation is not uniform across rooms, so the true clearStay spread is plausibly NARROWER than 49x - which would weaken rather than strengthen the case against a linear map. The exponent is still argued from data; it is argued from the wrong one of the four averages because it is the only one that has any. The 2026-08-14 real M7 did not help here either: its report was never written (see runloss-001), so it added no clearStay samples to the box. Revisit once clearStay has real samples, which is scores-fetch-001's downstream effect. NORMALISER: the median of the measured rooms, not the mean, because the distribution is not symmetric and one long room drags a mean far more than it moves a median; MEDIAN_BASE is ORDINARY_SEED itself rather than a second opinion, which is what makes the measured scale and the seed scale one scale. CLAMP: [0.25, 2.5] - a third of ordinary at the bottom (a room you cross in a moment is worth little and never nothing), 1.25x the largest seed at the top (measurement may say a room is harder than the hardest thing the user named, but not five times harder on one observation). Both are wide enough not to bind on ordinary rooms: at exponent 0.5 the top needs a room 11x the median. SHRINKAGE: k = 10 is the sample count at which measurement and seed weigh the same. n=1 moves a room 9% of the way, n=10 half, n=30 three quarters. At the box's current rate - 157 visits over 9 runs across 83 rooms - ten clears of one room is roughly forty runs, so a weight takes a season of play to turn over. That is the intended speed. Critically w is continuous in n, so there is NO CLIFF, and the guard asserts each step is no larger than the one before it rather than bounding steps by a threshold - which is why it catches a cliff wherever somebody puts one.

WHERE THE AVERAGES COME FROM: THREE LAYERS, BOTTOM TWO IMPLEMENTED. (1) freshly fetched - NOT BUILT, and deliberately not stubbed, because the receiver's do_GET answers /health and 404s everything else, so there is no endpoint to call. The mod-side feature is scores-fetch-001 in this list; the endpoint itself belongs on the receiver and the receiver goes first as always. (2) a cached file at configDir/sighteaddons/roomstats.json, read once per session, which is where the fetch will write. (3) the seeds. The FIRST DESIGN OF THIS FEATURE WAS A SNAPSHOT BUNDLED IN THE JAR and it was dropped mid-implementation on the user's push-back, which is right: if improving the values needs a jar release, they improve when somebody does release work rather than on their own, and that defeats the feature. The party-consistency argument for a bundled snapshot is real but small - the shrinkage means a room with many samples barely moves, so two clients days apart differ in a decimal rather than in a ranking. Nothing fetches anything; there is no network call in this feature. The file read is TOTAL: absent is the ordinary first case and yields exactly the seeds, malformed and truncated fall back the same way, and one broken entry costs its own room rather than the document.

WHICH NUMBER IS 'the average player clearing it, no secrets': roomstats.json's `clearStay`, not `clear`, not `afterClear`, not `secretRun`. clearStay is the minimum-stay anchor clear-001 ships; `clear` is the same span under the schema-4 anchor and is an upper bound a walk-through inflates; afterClear is the post-checkmark secret hunt and is exactly what 'KEINE SECRETS' excludes. Reading the wrong one is the silent failure on this feature - it produces plausible numbers off a metric that means something else - so it has its own test and its own mutation probe.

OLD AND NEW SCORES ARE NOT COMPARABLE AND NOTHING CONVERTS BETWEEN THEM. On the one real M7 there is, the old formula scored rooms from 1.00 (Hall) to 4.50 (Cathedral), and Pipes - a 1x4 holding seven secrets - was 1.0 + 7x0.25 + 3x0.5 = 4.25. THOSE FIGURES ARE NOW COMMITTED EVIDENCE RATHER THAN RELAYED PROSE, 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001: that M7 ran on a debug build of 72e0825, i.e. exactly the old formula, and its nine award events are at docs/evidence/session-1786719912927/session-excerpt.jsonl, summing to 26.25, with readout.sh asserting Hall 1.0, Cathedral 4.5, Pipes 4.25 and the sum. Until that commit these three numbers were cited as measurement in a source KDoc, a test KDoc and claude-progress.md with no reproducible provenance anywhere in the repository - their only source was an evaluator-rubric.md that has since been overwritten, which is what the clearpoints-002 evaluation docked Maintainability for. Note the direction of the check: the run corroborates the OLD formula, and no room in it had a measured clearStay average, so it says nothing about whether THIS model's numbers are right. Under this model Pipes seeds at 0.75 + 7x0.25 = 2.50, because its three extra segments stop being paid for. Every room came down and they came down by different amounts, so a per-player standing from an older build cannot be held next to one from this build. Stated in weightOf's KDoc, and pinned as a number against the real database by 'the seed weight of Pipes is the user's model, not the old one' - a reader looking for what changed will find an assertion rather than a comment.

WHICH SCORES A RUN USED IS RECORDED. Once layer 1 exists a run's points depend on when the player last launched, so RoomScores.generatedTs (0 for the seeds) rides on the `award` debug event, on a new `room_scores` debug event emitted when the resolution happens, and as a `scoresTs` key on every history.jsonl line. NOT on the run report: a key RUN_KEYS has not learned is an unknown key and a 400, and the report is where that rule bites. history.jsonl is the one permanent local file, and RoomHistory.fold reads by key, so the addition is invisible to every line already written.

NOT A SCHEMA CHANGE AND NOT PAIRED, verified against ingest.py this session rather than inherited from clearpoints-001's note: RUN_KEYS (ingest.py:137) and ROOM_KEYS (ingest.py:152) carry no per-player points field, so the whole breakdown never leaves the client and the weighting is invisible to the validator; `unattributed` is unchanged and still counted in ROOMS, not points, which is clearpoints-001's load-bearing half and must not be re-derived by subtraction. RunReport.kt is not touched by this branch at all and SCHEMA stays 5.

TWO EXISTING TESTS WERE REPLACED, DELIBERATELY, AND NEITHER WAS WEAKENED - see the second evidence entry for the exact accounting. Both pinned constants the user's model deletes; both replacements assert more than they did.

WHAT IS UNVERIFIED: the weights against a real run. Every property of the model is tested and mutation-probed, but that these numbers separate players in a way a player would agree with needs a floor played with the mod installed, which no command here can produce - it rides with ingame-001. And layer 2 has never been exercised by anything but a temp file: no cache has ever existed on a real install, because nothing writes one until scores-fetch-001 does.

SUPERSEDED IN ONE PLACE, 2026-08-14, BY scores-fetch-001 - the paragraph above beginning 'WHERE THE AVERAGES COME FROM' is history and is left as written. Layer 1 exists now: the receiver serves GET /roomstats (scores-002, deployed) and RoomStats fetches it at game start, caches it verbatim at configDir/sighteaddons/roomstats.json with its ETag beside it, and installs it for the session unless a run has already resolved. Nothing in THIS feature changed - the model, the seeds, the blend and RoomScores.parse are untouched - and layer 2 is now written by something rather than only by hand. The last line of the paragraph above ('no cache has ever existed on a real install') stays true until somebody launches a build carrying scores-fetch-001, which needs a release.

A late line needs the credit DEFERRED until the chat for that tick has been seen, which is a different change. WHAT CHAT CAN AND CANNOT SOURCE FOR SECRETS. Hypixel names a finder for exactly one kind of secret: the wither essence ('<name> found a Wither Essence! Everyone gains an extra essence!', and a second-person form for the local player). Chests, levers, item pickups and the redstone key are announced NOWHERE -- the action bar's per-room counter is the only signal and it says 'somebody', never who. So SecretTracker.isOwn's 40-tick coincidence STAYS, and chat narrows it rather than replacing it: where a line names somebody the inference is not consulted, everywhere else nothing changed. What that buys is the FALSE POSITIVE -- a teammate taking the essence while your own click on a chest is still inside its window used to credit you.

NOT PAIRED, AND THAT WAS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A DISCOVERY. Deaths feed the existing `deaths` and per-room `deaths`; essence attribution feeds the existing `ownSecrets`. UNVERIFIED, AND NOT SMALL. (1) THAT THE STRINGS ARE HYPIXEL'S. Every shape is cited to a published mod that runs against the live server -- SkyHanni, Cowlection's DungeonsListener, UnclaimedBloom6/IllegalMap, inglettronald/DulkirMod, odtheking/OdinLegacy -- which is the standard SECRET_SKULLS is already held to, and it is not the same as having seen one. A wrong pattern fails silently and benignly: it matches nothing and the mod goes on inferring exactly as before. The receiver's agent/AGENT-PROMPT.md line 62 tells its analysis agent to look for '`unattributed` large relative to `roomsCleared` in `run_end`' — that gap is the documented diagnostic for a broken decoration->player mapping. The mod's run_end event (SighteAddons.kt:149) writes floor, roomsCleared, points, unnamed and newRecords, and NOT unattributed. So the receiver's runbook names a field that has never been in the log, and an analyst following it finds a hole rather than a signal. This is a one-field addition to a debug event: not a schema change, not paired (DebugLog is the mod's own JSONL and the receiver does not validate it), and no version bump. Worth doing deliberately anyway, because the alternative reading is that AGENT-PROMPT.md meant the per-room `unattributed` EVENT that award() emits, in which case the fix is on the receiver's side of the wire and is a different delegation — decide which before writing the line. Note also that the per-room `unattributed` event fires whenever the MIN_TICKS split was empty, including when the raw-presence fallback then credited somebody, so counting those events is NOT the same number as the run's unattributed rooms; whoever picks this up should say which of the two the analyst wants.

features.notes:
FIXED AT cd26786, ON BRANCH runloss-001, NOT MERGED AND NOT PUSHED. The history below is kept because it is the only record of what the defect cost; what changed is at the end.

MEASURED DATA LOSS, NOT A THEORETICAL ONE. Recorded 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001, which found it while reading the first real session file rather than while looking for it.

WHAT HAPPENED. The user played a real M7 on 2026-08-14 (docs/evidence/session-1786719912927/) and quit the game straight from the dungeon. The session file carries NO `run_end` event, no run report was written, and runs/uploaded/'s newest file predates the run by a day, so the receiver got nothing. Ten cleared rooms, permanently gone from the box. readout.sh asserts run_end = 0.

WHAT SURVIVED. history.jsonl got 14 lines from that run, because RoomHistory appends and flushes per line. The local records were intact; only the REPORT was lost.

WHAT THE FIX IS. ClientPlayConnectionEvents.DISCONNECT is now a third call site for RunReport.write, alongside the end-of-run headline and JOIN. Three things had to be settled first, and the ponytail note was right that none of them was a one-liner:

1. THE PLAYER IS NOT RELIABLY RESOLVABLE THERE, AND THIS IS MEASURED. Minecraft.destroy() disconnects the level before disconnectWithProgressScreen(); Connection.disconnect is channel.close().awaitUninterruptibly(); Fabric raises DISCONNECT from a HEAD inject on Connection.channelInactive with no hop to the client thread; and Netty completes the close future before firing channelInactive, so the handler races `this.player = null` from another thread. The answer was to stop asking the client: PartyTracker.localName holds the name, captured every second of the run, and it is also the name every room's tick map is keyed by - so it is the more correct source, not a fallback. RunReport.uploader carries the whole measurement in its KDoc with the javap commands to recheck it.

2. A HALF-WRITTEN REPORT IS WORSE THAN NONE. The write happens a few statements before System.exit(0). A truncated run-*.json still matches TelemetryUpload.RUN, is posted at the next launch, fails check_run with a 400 and lives in rejected/ for good. Reports now go through the same .part + atomic move restamp already used; `.part` is outside the uploader's pattern by construction.

3. summaryPrinted WAS NOT ENOUGH. It is only ever set by the headline, so it cannot see the pair DISCONNECT introduces: dropping to the title screen from inside a floor writes the report, and joining any server afterwards reaches JOIN with nothing having reset in between - two reports for one run. The guard moved into RunReport, is claimed before the write, given back if the write fails, and cleared by DungeonSession.reset().

WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED, AND IS NOT IMPLIED TO BE. A hard kill (task manager, SIGKILL, power loss) runs nothing at all and loses the run exactly as before. A Java-level crash that still reaches Minecraft.destroy() is covered by the same disconnect, but that is read off destroy()'s bytecode and has never been observed. A JVM shutdown hook was considered and rejected: it cannot help with SIGKILL, DISCONNECT already fires before System.exit(0) on every path that reaches destroy(), and a second writer racing the first would buy nothing that RunReport.reported does not already have to arbitrate.

WHAT IS UNVERIFIED. That the Fabric event fires at all on a real quit. The dev client cannot reach Hypixel and the event cannot be raised in a unit test, so the wiring rests on the disassembly above and on nothing else. verification_manual is the procedure that turns it into a measurement, and the new `run_report` debug event is what it looks for.

NOT A SCHEMA CHANGE AND NOT PAIRED, confirmed rather than assumed: build/keydiff.py reports four empty sets both directions, before and after. RunReport.SCHEMA stays 5.

RELATIONSHIP TO runend-001: unchanged. runend-001 adds a FIELD to the run_end event; this was about the report not happening at all.

features.notes:
THE BLOCKER IS GONE, AND IT WAS THE RECEIVER'S TO CLEAR. `scores-002` on Sighte/skyblock-server is passing and deployed: GET /roomstats answers 200 with the document and an ETag, 304 on If-None-Match, 503 with `no scores document` when there is nothing to serve or it does not parse, and 404 for every other path - /roomstats.json, /roomstats/, /roomstats?v=1 and a POST included, because the match is exact. No token, by decision: the store is aggregate per room and carries no install id or player name, and a token compiled into a published jar would not be a secret, it would only cost the endpoint its cacheability. Verified from here rather than taken on trust - see the curl evidence entry and the live probe.

WHAT WAS BUILT: LAYER 1 AND NOTHING ELSE. RoomStats.start() at game start, fetch, cache verbatim, install for this session. Layers 2 and 3 are untouched and RoomScores.parse did not need a line - it already read the receiver's document verbatim, which is what made this wiring rather than surgery.

THE PATTERN IS TelemetryUpload'S, DELIBERATELY, NOT A SECOND ONE: a named daemon thread started from onInitializeClient, everything inside it wrapped, nothing on the client thread and nothing during a run. Its own thread rather than a step inside the upload's, because the upload hands over a backlog of run reports at 60 s a file and the scores would then arrive after the first room of the evening rather than before it.

A DOCUMENT THAT ARRIVES LATE IS CACHED AND NOT ADOPTED, and that refusal is the feature rather than a safety net. A room's weight is read at the moment it is cleared and points are compared between party members, so scores that changed halfway through a run would make its second half incomparable with its first and with the other four players'. RoomStats.adopt returns false once the session has resolved; the document is already in the cache by then, so it is what the next launch reads. The resolution, adopt and use are all synchronised on RoomStats now, because the fetch runs on another thread and that race is a run scored against two weightings.

THE ETAG IS PERSISTED BESIDE THE CACHE at roomstats.etag, not inside it: the cache is the receiver's bytes verbatim and a wrapper object would be exactly the transform RoomScores.parse exists to avoid. TWO HALVES OF ONE GUARD: the document is written BEFORE the tag, and cachedEtag returns null whenever the document is not on disk. An ETag naming bytes that are not there earns a 304, and a 304 with no cache behind it is a session on the seeds - at every launch, until the receiver's document happened to change. That is the one shape of this that could wedge an install permanently, so it is guarded at both ends and has its own case and its own probe.

FAILURE IS THE ORDINARY CASE. Nine shapes are driven through the real client in one test and none of them throws or touches the cache; the tenth, a dead host, is a port that was bound to find a free one and released again. Logged at INFO rather than WARN on purpose - a box that is down, a player with no connection and a receiver too old to know this path are all ordinary and all cost nothing but freshness.

GATED ON THE /sa UPLOAD SWITCH, WHICH IS A DECISION AND IS REVERSIBLE IN ONE LINE. The switch is worded about SENDING reports and this request sends nothing but a revalidation header, so gating is the conservative reading rather than a required one - but it is the only control a player has over whether this mod talks to the analysis server at all, and a launch that quietly contacts it anyway would make the one-time disclosure less true than it reads. The cost is that such an install keeps its cached scores or its seeds, which is exactly the behaviour before this feature existed, and that two party members can then be on different weightings - a decimal rather than a ranking, by clearpoints-002's shrinkage argument. If the user wants the other trade, delete the `if (!Config.upload) return` at the top of RoomStats.start().

THE BODY IS READ BOUNDED (8 MB) because it is the only body of unknown length this mod reads off a network. The cap is a parameter of fetch() purely so a test does not have to serve eight megabytes to prove it.

TelemetryUpload.PUBLIC_URL IS INTERNAL NOW so one host lives in one constant. The public base on purpose even for an install with an upload.properties: /roomstats needs no token and serves the same aggregate document to everybody, so the private tier's URL would only decide which box an author reads scores from, which is not a question that file is answering.

NOT A SCHEMA CHANGE AND NOT PAIRED - verified with the key diff rather than assumed. No report field was added, RunReport.kt is not in this branch's diff at all, and SCHEMA stays 5. generatedTs already rides on the `award` and `room_scores` debug events and on every history.jsonl line (clearpoints-002 built that), and a fetched document keeps it true because adopt installs the parsed RoomScores whose generatedTs is the document's - pinned by the first evidence entry's case. A new `room_scores_fetch` debug event records the outcome, the reason when it failed, the generatedTs when it did not, and how long it took.

WHAT THE RECEIVER'S scores-002 NOTES ASK FOR AND THIS DOES NOT DO: 'prefer the served `score` over the one it computes'. The document carries a `scores` block of resolved per-room scores alongside the `rooms` array of raw averages, and this feature reads the averages and keeps clearpoints-002's model on the client, which is what the mod-side brief asked for. Moving the model to the server is a real design question - it would make every client agree exactly, and it would also make a weight unexplainable from the jar - and it is NOT recorded as a feature here because it is a decision rather than an omission. Raise it with the user.

WHAT IS UNVERIFIED, AND THE FIRST ONE IS THE CEILING: no real client has ever done this. The dev client cannot reach Hypixel, so RoomStats.start() has never run inside a game - what IS measured is every piece it calls, against the live box, through the mod's own code (see the live-probe entry). What a real launch would show is a room_scores_fetch line and then a room_scores line with source 'fetch' in the session file, and a roomstats.json in config/sighteaddons/. Second: the MEASURED HALF OF THE MODEL IS STILL INERT. The live document has 105 rooms and sampled 0 - every clearStay is n=0 - because no schema 5 build has been RELEASED, so every score in it is exactly seed plus secrets. Fetching does not change that; what it changes is that every LATER improvement no longer needs a jar. features.user_visible_behavior: The analyst can see who opened which wither door, who solved and who failed each puzzle, and which secrets were whose -- from the permanent run report rather than only from a debug session that the player can switch off and that is capped at 20 000 events.
verification_manual: After the receiver is deployed, play a floor and confirm the report is accepted rather than landing in rejected/.
features.blocked_reason: THE RECEIVER GOES FIRST, and its feature does not exist yet. chat-001 already reads these events (wither_door, blood_door, puzzle_solved, puzzle_failed, and a named finder per essence secret) and writes them to the debug log only. Unblocking needs, IN THIS ORDER: (1) a feature in Sighte/skyblock-server adding the chosen keys to RUN_KEYS/ROOM_KEYS or their optional sets with validators, reaching `passing`; (2) that change DEPLOYED to master, which is the user's decision and not a session's; (3) only then this, with a SCHEMA bump if any existing key changes meaning. Note the receiver's own ceilings while choosing the shape (MAX_SECRETS 64, MAX_DEATHS 500) and that a per-player secret breakdown puts TEAMMATE NAMES in a permanent server-side record, which RunReport's header refuses on purpose -- so it would have to be per-slot or per-class, not per-name. That question is why this is a feature and not a follow-up commit.
features.notes: Raised by chat-001, 2026-08-14, rather than built inside it. The unpaired shape was available and was taken: deaths and essence attribution improve numbers the receiver already accepts (`deaths`, room `deaths`, `ownSecrets`), so chat-001 moved no field and needed no receiver change. This entry is only the part that cannot be done that way. features.title: Log whether the dungeon map's decorations carry a name
features.user_visible_behavior: Nothing visible. One extra field in an existing debug event, so that the next real party floor answers a question no amount of reading can.
verification_manual: Play a floor with at least two people and the debug log on.
Read `player_room` in the session file: if `decoName` is null on every event, `MapDecoration.name()` is not populated by Hypixel and `party-001` should be closed.
If it is not null, record exactly what it contains before anything reads it.
features.notes:
Recorded rather than built, per CLAUDE.md's rule about work discovered mid-feature. `party-001` established that no key survives the wire (see its evidence) and that `MapDecoration.name()` (`Optional<Component>`) is the ONLY per-decoration identity channel left in the 26.1.2 protocol. Whether Hypixel populates it is unknowable from this machine. This is one field on the existing `player_room` event in `PartyTracker.positions`, next to decoType/decoX/decoY.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THAT MAKES IT A FEATURE AND NOT A COMMIT: if the name is populated it is most likely the teammate's IGN, and a raw IGN must not reach the debug log - `Pseudonym` exists precisely so the log never carries a stranger's name. So the field has to be redacted on the way in, and a redacted value cannot tell you what the name WAS, which is the thing this feature is trying to find out. `Pseudonym.row`'s existing answer applies: replace anything name-shaped and keep the rest, so the log says whether there was a name and what shape it had without saying whose. Decide that before writing the field, not after.

Only worth doing if somebody is going to play a party floor. It proves nothing on its own and it cannot be verified here.

features.notes:
MEASURED ON THE BOX, 2026-08-15. Of 22 uploaded reports, 20 carry floor `?` and only 2 carry a real floor - and both of those are v4/0.9.0. In roomstats.json, 115 of 125 room entries are grouped under `?`. This is not old data: the three newest reports are v5, one of them from the 0.10.0 release, and all three say `?`.

THE CAUSE, and it is one line doing two jobs. DungeonSession.kt:61 is
  floor = sidebarLines(client).firstNotNullOfOrNull { FLOOR.find(it)?.groupValues?.get(1) }
  return floor != null
That assignment IS the in-dungeon check, so every call outside a dungeon overwrites a known floor with null. RunReport.kt:171 then reads `DungeonSession.floor ?: "?"`. The report is written on ClientPlayConnectionEvents.JOIN - after leaving - so by then the value is gone. The two reports that DO carry M7 are the ones written from the run-end headline, while the player was still inside and the sidebar still showed it. The check that asks whether you are still in a dungeon destroys the fact the report needs.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: roomstats groups every room entry by floor, so the fold cannot separate a room that is genuinely harder on F7 from the same room on F5 even if somebody wanted it to. records-001 was deferred by the user on the grounds that per-floor judgement is too much work - worth knowing that the data would not currently support it either way. The scoring model does not read floor and is unaffected.

SHAPE OF THE FIX, not prescribed: keep the last known floor for the life of a run rather than letting the detector clear it, and clear it in DungeonSession.reset() where the run actually ends. Check runloss-001's DISCONNECT path too - it writes off-thread and must see the same value.

NOT PAIRED: `floor` is already in RUN_KEYS and the receiver validates it today. This changes the value, not the shape.

FIXED 2026-08-15 at c6142d4. The shape is the one the diagnosis proposed. `inDungeon(client)` is now `observeSidebar(sidebarLines(client))`, and `observeSidebar` does the two jobs separately: it answers about NOW (`return seen != null`, so the session state machine in onTick still stops the moment the sidebar stops naming a floor) and it only ever WRITES a floor it actually saw. Nothing else clears the field; `DungeonSession.reset()` does, and reset() runs on JOIN *after* the JOIN site has written the report for the run being left. `floor` is `@Volatile` now because the DISCONNECT path reads it from a Netty event-loop thread - the same reason RunReport.reported is an AtomicBoolean. `RunReport.reportedFloor()` names the read all three write paths share, because RunReport.write() needs a live Minecraft and cannot be called from this suite at all - which is how a one-line defect survived five schema versions with 184 tests around it.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED: every one of the three paths, end to end. The dev client cannot log in, so no real report has been written under this code. What the suite measures is the whole of the remember/forget/answer decision on real sidebar strings, and that the report reads the remembered value; what it cannot measure is that the sidebar in a real Hypixel dungeon is read by `sidebarLines` at all (unchanged by this feature and evidenced by the two reports on the box that DO carry M7), and that reset() lands on the JOIN edge of every real run. Also unverified in the strict sense: `@Volatile` gives visibility, but no test can observe its absence reliably - the modifier is asserted by reflection instead.

DISCOVERED, NOT FIXED: the receiver's FLOOR validator accepts `?|E|[FM][1-7]` and this mod can produce the string `Entrance`. See floorname-001. Measured as unreachable today - a report needs a non-empty room list, which needs calibration inside a floor instance, where the sidebar reads F/M - so this fix does not open it. It is recorded rather than patched inline.

features.title: The mod cannot send a floor the receiver would reject
features.user_visible_behavior: A run played anywhere the sidebar names is uploaded rather than 400'd away, so no run is lost to a floor string the two sides spell differently.
verification_manual: Diff the value domain, not just the key set: every string DungeonSession.floor can hold against ingest.py's FLOOR pattern.
features.notes:
FOUND WHILE FIXING floorloss-001, 2026-08-15, and deliberately not fixed inline.

The receiver validates `floor` with FLOOR = re.compile(r"\?|E|[FM][1-7]") under fullmatch (ingest.py:93, used at ingest.py:225). The mod's own FLOOR regex is Regex("""The Catacombs \((\w+)\)""") and DungeonSession.floor's own KDoc has said since it was written that the values are "F7", "M7" or "Entrance". `Entrance` does not fullmatch that pattern - the receiver clearly expected `E`. A report carrying it is a 400, and TelemetryUpload never retries a 400, so the run is gone.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT, measured rather than assumed: RunReport.write returns early on an empty room list, rooms are only ever added by ContributionTracker.tick, and that only runs once DungeonSession.update has calibrated against the Mort armor stand and the dungeon map - which exists only inside a floor instance, where the sidebar reads (F7)/(M7). The Catacombs Entrance is a separate Hypixel server, so arriving there is a JOIN and a reset. So no report with rooms in it can currently carry `Entrance`. floorloss-001 does not widen this: the floor is cleared on every JOIN either way.

WHAT THE WORK IS. Decide which side spells it, then make the two agree and TEST THE AGREEMENT rather than restating it. The cheap half is on this side (map `Entrance` -> `E` at the one point that files it, RunReport.reportedFloor) and needs no receiver change, no schema move and no pairing. The other half - teaching the validator the long spelling - is a receiver feature and would be paired. Prefer the first: `E` is already the shape the receiver's own regex was written for.

WORTH KNOWING EITHER WAY: build/keydiff.py compares KEY SETS and is clean here. It cannot see a value-domain mismatch, and this is the first one anybody has hit. That is a gap in the check, not a failure of it.

features.title: The near-miss log can be read
features.user_visible_behavior: A session file shows which Hypixel lines a chat pattern failed to match, instead of drowning them in party chatter with every word replaced by a pseudonym.
verification_manual: Play a floor with a talkative party and confirm chat_unparsed carries dungeon lines, not player sentences.
features.notes:
MEASURED, 2026-08-15, from three real M7 party runs on 0.10.0/0.11.0. 32 chat_unparsed events, and the sample is entirely PLAYER CHAT rather than unmatched Hypixel lines - e.g. '[p-bed304e3] p-3b5d9203 p-ae727fc2 p-347caa5c: I am p-3b5d9203 p-ae727fc2 p-347caa5c. I p-ad5d88b2 p-7c278c05'. Two defects in one line.

(1) The near-miss log records lines a human typed. Those can never match a dungeon pattern, so they are noise in the one place built to diagnose a pattern that stopped matching - chat-001's own recorded purpose for it.

(2) Pseudonym.row is applied to free chat text, so EVERY whitespace token becomes a pseudonym - 'I am ...' reads as three player ids. That is over-redaction rather than a leak, so it is not a privacy defect; but it makes the log unreadable for the diagnosis it exists for. Note this cuts both ways and the fix must not become an under-redaction: a player sentence can contain another player's name, which is exactly what Pseudonym exists to keep out of a permanent log.

SHAPE: skip lines that carry a chat prefix (a speaker before a colon) before logging a near miss, or log only lines that reached a pattern and failed. Not paired - DebugLog bodies are never parsed by the receiver (ingest.py validates the filename only).
